comment: Bizar assigns one exact gateway model to each shipped agent. Role selection and complexity/model selection are separate decisions; every run snapshots its assignments before dispatch. Premium orchestrator/debug/planning tier uses Qwen 3.8 Max via the 9router gateway; MiniMax tiers are routed as claude-minimax/* gateway IDs.

premium.purpose: Primary orchestration, system planning, and last-resort debugging where reasoning quality dominates cost. Qwen 3.8 Max is reserved for the user-facing orchestrator, planning, and Carl escalation.

high.purpose: Complex implementation and adversarial review where mistakes are expensive.

default.purpose: Broad, high-throughput research and guarded delivery operations.

mid.purpose: Bounded technical analysis, code search, and moderate implementation.

budget.purpose: Deterministic edits, clarification, and mechanical verification.

orchestration.purpose: The single primary entrypoint; decomposes, dispatches, coordinates, and synthesizes without implementing.

research.purpose: Repository mapping and official-documentation evidence gathering.

planning.purpose: Turn researched facts into reversible, testable implementation plans.

clarification.purpose: Ask one high-value question only when missing information materially blocks the plan.

implementation.purpose: Implement approved work at complexity-appropriate depth.

debugging.purpose: Resolve failures that survived lower-cost debugging passes.

design.purpose: Define and audit product visual language and interaction quality.

verification.purpose: Collect browser and user-facing behavior evidence.

support.purpose: Answer read-only project questions with source references.

delivery.purpose: Perform approval-gated Git and external delivery operations.

mike.rationale: The sole main orchestrator the user talks to; Qwen 3.8 Max sustains cross-phase decomposition, coordination, and synthesis without losing project constraints.

paul.rationale: System-wide plans and reversible execution boundaries require the strongest long-horizon reasoning; shares the user-facing orchestrator tier.

carl.rationale: Last-resort debugging is reserved for novel cross-cutting failures; Qwen 3.8 Max gives Carl the same headroom as the user-facing orchestrator.

karen.rationale: Complex implementation and architecture work need high reasoning while preserving a distinct escalation tier.

linda.rationale: Adversarial review needs strong independent reasoning to detect plan, security, and verification gaps.

brad.rationale: Brand systems benefit from a focused design model rather than general implementation capacity.

ria.rationale: UI critique, interaction detail, and accessibility review align with the focused design tier.

greg.rationale: Repository and official-documentation research needs broad context handling at high throughput.

steve.rationale: Guarded Git and delivery operations need dependable command reasoning more than speculative depth.

todd.rationale: Moderate implementation is bounded enough for the mid tier while still requiring technical judgment.

oscar.rationale: Intent-based code discovery is a bounded technical analysis task with concrete evidence checks.

susan.rationale: Source-grounded project explanations need enough reasoning to connect code paths without implementation overhead.

brenda.rationale: Routine deterministic edits and maintenance should use the lowest capable model.

pam.rationale: Single-shot mechanical tasks are intentionally constrained to the budget model.

janet.rationale: One targeted clarification is a narrow task that does not justify a higher reasoning tier.

kevin.rationale: Scripted browser verification is mechanical and evidence-driven.
